LESSON: SIGN READING 3.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: SKIMMING AND SCANNING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Sign Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Skimming and Scanning
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Skimming and Scanning, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we read? 2. Why do we sign read? 3. How can we read faster? 4. How can we sign read faster?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize signs of words and phrases related to the theme.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Skimming and Scanning in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. sign read a text of about 300 words for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Skimming and Scanning in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply appropriate reading and sign reading skills when reading a text of about 300 words to obtain both factual and inferential information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Skimming and Scanning in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of intensive reading in their day-to-day life. ● In pairs, learners are guided to watch a captioned video clip or observe a signed demonstration of vocabulary related to etiquette. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to etiquette. ● In groups, learners are guided to sign read and read a variety of print and non-print texts of about 300 words for comprehension. ● In groups, learners are guided to identify events in a story or a passage of about 300 words with logical and fluent flow. ● In groups, learners are guided to answer factual and inferential questions from a text of about 300 words. ● In pairs, learners are guided to work together to infer the meaning of vocabulary from contexts. ● In groups, learners are guided to skim through a digital text of about 300 words focusing mainly on the title and illustrations. ● In pairs, learners are guided to scan for information such as words and answer questions from print or digital text. ● In pairs, learners are guided to skim or scan a comic, magazine, newspaper or age- appropriate reader. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Skimming and Scanning together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner works collaboratively with peers during a group discussion.

● Digital literacy: learner independently interacts with digital devices to sign read texts.

Values:
● Peace is developed as the learners use polite language and etiquette to avoid hurting others.

● Respect is developed as the learner is able to demonstrate etiquette when dealing with peers in class.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to connect the concept of etiquette and politeness to their learning in Integrated Science.
